This is the kind of dinner that starts with an onion and ends with something deeply savoury, without asking you to babysit a pot for hours. The beans do most of the work.
Use a good tinned tomato and a generous amount of olive oil. The stew is even better the next day, so it is worth making a double batch on Sunday.
Ingredients
Two tablespoons of olive oil
One large yellow onion, diced
Three cloves of garlic, sliced
Two tins of cannellini beans
One tin of whole peeled tomatoes
A small bunch of flat-leaf parsley
Method
Warm the olive oil in a heavy pot over medium heat, then cook the onion with a pinch of salt until it is soft and translucent, about eight minutes.
Add the garlic and cook for one more minute, stirring so it does not brown, then tip in the tomatoes and break them up with a wooden spoon.
Drain and rinse the beans, add them to the pot with a splash of water, and simmer uncovered for twenty minutes until the liquid thickens around the beans.
Taste and adjust the salt, scatter the chopped parsley over the top, and serve with toasted bread or rice.
Cook's notes
If you have a parmesan rind, drop it in with the tomatoes and fish it out before serving.
